good evening chair donahue and miss mansfield and miss labelle i am pleased to be here to give you just a brief overview of our draft regulation for policy 6640. on our first slide we have basically just a description of what our AED and medical emergency response teams are in our schools, as well as how they are made up, and their roles, the trainings, and the drills that are conducted within those teams annually.

This slide shows the diabetes medical management plan, otherwise referred to as the DMMP. That must be completed by the health care provider and signed by parents each year. A new DMMP, an addendum, or written orders are required for additions or changes to a student's DMMP.

Parents are responsible for obtaining any additions or changes from the health care provider. The DMMP is reviewed by the resource nurse or school nurse for clarity. The resource nurse or school nurse contacts the medical provider if there are questions or further information is needed.

Once the DMMP is approved, the resource nurse or school nurse, parents and guardians, and any unlicensed trained staff and teachers who have responsibility for the child at that school meet to discuss the DMMP to determine the individual needs of the student.

This information is then incorporated and developed into a classroom emergency action plan, otherwise referred to as an EAP. The EAP will be reviewed with those teachers and staff who have direct care of the student.

If the student rides a school bus, transportation and the bus driver will be informed of the student's diagnosis and a resource nurse or school nurse will review the EAP with the bus driver. This slide goes into detail about the training and the different levels of trainings offered in accordance with the recommendations from the Virginia Department of Education Diabetes Management in Schools.

And you see there is a level one training, a level two training, as well as a level three training. Next slide, please. This slide goes into further detail and provides information pertaining to continuous glucose monitors, otherwise known as CGMs, and insulin pumps.

Parents and guardians may demonstrate the use of CGMs and insulin pumps at schools. The slide also indicates the training necessary to administer insulin and glucagon to students in accordance with the Virginia Department of Education manual for training of public school employees in the administration of insulin and glucagon.

This slide describes the use of an insulin pump. Due to different models and functions of insulin pumps, parents and guardians are asked to perform all basic setup and maintenance care at home. If the pump malfunctions, becomes dislodged, or comes off of the body, insulin will be administered in accordance with the DMMP.

If the student has been identified per the DMMP as independent in reinsertion skills, he or she may reinsert the infusion set or pump. If the student is not independent and parents and guardians are unable to come to the school, insulin will be administered by insulin vial and syringe or insulin pen as per the DMMP.
